_doc: Apple Trade-In max published values per model id. Refreshed weekly by scripts/refresh-apple-comps.py via .github/workflows/refresh-comps.yml (the scraper currently reads nothing useful, see _verification). Frontend reads this at runtime when device is in the Apple family. CONVENTION: only include a value Apple's own trade-in estimator actually shows. notAccepted = model ids a manual check confirmed Apple's estimator does NOT list; only those get the 'Apple won't take this on trade-in' claim. A model with no value and not in notAccepted makes no claim either way.

_verification.2026-09-16: Manual check (Powerhouse). iPhone values = maxValue per model from Apple's public estimator (www.apple.com/shop/tradein-module, Smartphone > Apple); ip17air uses the landing-page table's 'iPhone Air Up to $585' (the estimator said $560; the higher number keeps 'we pay more' claims true). aw_ultra3 and aw_s10 = the landing-page Apple Watch table rows (Ultra 3 $430, Series 10 $150). iPhone 17e, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo are not in the estimator's model list -> notAccepted. PR #4's ip16pm/ip16p = 720 was the scraper reading one page-wide 'Up to $720'; the estimator shows 610/510.
_verification.watches: aw_ultra2 265, aw_ultra 190, aw_s9 115, aw_s8 90, aw_s7 65 (and aw_ultra3 430, aw_s10 150, aw_se2022 60 unchanged) = Apple's per-model maxima in MacRumors' 2026-09-15 trade-in table, whose iPhone rows match the estimator values above exactly.
_verification.added: ip13mini 145, aw_s11 200, aw_se3 115 = the iPhone 13 mini, Apple Watch Series 11 and Apple Watch SE (3rd generation) rows of MacRumors' 2026-09-15 table (9to5Mac 2026-09-09 lists the same); they were missing, so the homepage told 13 mini / Series 11 / SE 3 sellers Apple publishes no price. The homepage's watch ids (awu3, aws10, ...) map onto these aw_* keys in app/page.tsx (APPLE_WATCH_COMP_ID).
_verification.unverified: Mac, iPad and aw_se2024 values are still the 2026-06-22 snapshot: Apple's estimator asks for a serial number before it shows a per-model Mac/iPad value, and MacRumors lists only family maxima (2026-09-16 / 09-15: MacBook Pro $1315, MacBook Air $705, iPad Pro $905, iPad Air $510, iPad mini $320, iPad $280). Apple RAISED Mac and iPad values on 2026-08-06 and 2026-09-15, so these snapshots likely sit low; /sell makes no iPad/Mac claim from them (see goodConditionFloor in app/sell/[slug]/page.tsx).
